newsitem.title: USA: Jewell reaches settlement with CNN -lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Jewell reaches settlement with CNN -lawyer.

text.p: Attorneys for Richard Jewell said on Tuesday they reached a settlement with Cable News Network over claims that the 24-hour news channel invaded the privacy of the former security guard and his mother during its coverage of last summer's Olympic park bombing.

"We have reached a settlement with CNN. That is actually going to be physically consummated this afternoon," said Lin Wood, one of two civil lawyers retained by Jewell. CNN, which operates as a unit of media giant Time Warner Inc., had no immediate comment.

"The amount of the settlement is both confidential and, under the terms of the agreement, cannot be characterised, except for me to tell you that it was a monetary payment to Barbara Jewell, the mother, and Richard Jewell," said Wood.

Jewell already has reached an out-of-court settlement with the NBC network, which is owned by General Electric Co. An unconfirmed report by the Wall Street Journal put the value of that deal at more than $500,000.
"As with NBC, I think it's a safe assumption that both sides are again in this instance mutually satisfied with the settlement," the attorney added.

Jewell's attorneys contended that the news channel violated Georgia state privacy laws by posting a camera and a surveillance car outside the family apartment for about a month after a federal search of the residence on July 31.
